WYESIDE IS 50 — AND YOU'RE INVITED

For 50 years, people have come through Wyeside's doors to meet friends and share experiences. 

For 3 days 9 October - 11 October, we are going back to the start to the 70’s to revisit some classic films including Bedknobs and Broomsticks, Jaws and so many more. 

Progress into the noughties, where you might see yourself on screen as we bring you the story of Builth told in BWCAS: A Little Bit of Heaven - with a cast of over 80 local stars. 

And in this decade we introduce you to some fabulous new live music from Cardinal Sin and Bryde, poetry from Owen Sheers, and we celebrate our namesake - the River Wye in our gallery exhibition.

We are also delighted to announce new music commissioned especially for our anniversary!

Don’t miss out on 70’s inspired cocktails and some delicious food to enjoy from Beefy Boys, Mozzarella Fella and The Diner. 

Come for one event. Stay for several. Help us celebrate 50 years of Wyeside as we plan for a brilliant future together. 

  • Bedknobs & Broomsticks (PG)

    Friday 9 October | 4:30pm

    Animation | Adventure | Comedy | Family | Fantasy | Musical

    An apprentice witch, three kids, and a cynical magician conman search for the missing component to a magic spell to be used in the defence of Britain in World War II.

    Running Time: 117 mins | Flashing Images: None

    Tickets: £5 (plus £1 admin fee)

    Book Now

  • Gallery Exhibition Opening

    What Does The River Wye Mean To You?

    Friday 9 October | 6pm

    9 October - 16 December | Free Entry

    This exhibition, by local artists, pays tribute to the River Wye and the important role it plays in shaping our landscape, culture and heritage.

    The artwork is inspired by the Wye’s nature, the flora and fauna of the river and the rich folklore and tales centred around its powerful, mysterious even magical qualities.

    The rich tapestry of artwork exhibited is testament to how our local communities are touched by the Wye.

    More Information to come

  • Taxi Driver (18)

    Friday 9 October | 7:15pm

    Crime | Drama

    A mentally unstable veteran works as a night-time taxi driver in New York City, where the perceived decadence and sleaze fuels his urge for violent action.

    Running Time: 114 mins | Flashing Images: None

    Tickets: £5 (plus £1 admin fee)

    Book Now

  • Cardinal Sin with support from Ophelia's Beard

    Friday 9 October | 7:30pm

    Get ready to dance!

    Cardinal Sin are a 4 piece Alt Country Rock band from South Wales. The band have spent the last year tucked away in the Black Mountains writing and carving their sound.

    Their music is heavily inspired by their surroundings and influenced by the all new Americana & Country scene.

    Tickets: £10 (plus £1 admin fee)

    Book Now

  • Photographic History of Wyeside

    Saturday 10 October | 12:15pm

    One hundred and fifty years ago this year the people of Builth decided that their town needed a building dedicated to staging live music. Fifty years ago this year that idea evolved into a vision of creating Builth’s very own Art Centre.

    Today the Wyeside Art Centre has become a beloved part of the lives and memories of many of the town’s inhabitants. This is the story of the journey in-between, through good times and bad, and of the story of Builth’s very own centre for the arts.

    Tickets: £2 (plus £1 admin fee)

    Book Now

  • Bugsy Malone (U)

    Saturday 10 October | 1pm

    Comedy | Crime | Family | Musical

    The classic gangster story of Bugsy Malone told with an all-child cast. The rise of Bugsy Malone and the battle for power between gangsters Fat Sam and Dandy Dan.

    Running Time: 94 mins | Flashing Images: None

    Tickets: £5 (plus £1 admin fee)

    Book Now

  • Owen Sheers

    Saturday 10 October | 2pm

    An afternoon of poetry from twice-winner of Wales Book of the Year, Owen Sheers.

    Owen is a poet, author and playwright whose awards for poetry include the Society of Authors Somerset Maugham award (for Skirrid Hill), the Hay Poetry Medal and the Wilfred Owen Poetry Award.

    Owen will read from a selection of existing and new work, followed by a Q&A and book signing. 

    Tickets: £10 (plus £1 admin fee)

    Book Now

  • BWCAS: A Little Below Heaven

    Saturday 10 October | 3:30pm

    Come along and see the film that Builth Wells Community Arts Society created all those years ago!

    This short film has not been seen since 2002…

    Did you or someone you know take part?

    Tickets: £2 (plus £1 admin fee)

    Book Now

  • Afon Llynfi - Artist Talk

    Saturday 10 October | 4pm

    Artist Beverley Thornley will talk about her explorations of the Afon Llynfi and the paintings and books she has made of this tributary of the Wye. Collecting minerals and motifs and using them to depict places and environmental change is the bedrock of Beverley’s practice.

    In this case she has collected old red sandstone, oak galls and alder cones for the ink used in her paintings.  She will show how this is done and be selling and signing her artist book Notes on a River - Afon Llynfi. Proceeds will be donated to Friends of the River Wye.

    Includes talk, Q&A and book signing.

    Tickets: Free

    Book Now

  • Jaws (12A)

    Saturday 10 October | 7pm

    Adventure | Drama | Horror | Thriller

    They are going to need a bigger boat!

    When a massive killer shark unleashes chaos on a beach community off Long Island, it's up to the local police chief, a marine biologist, and an old seafarer to hunt the beast down.

    Running Time: 124 mins | Flashing Images: None

    Tickets: £5 (plus £1 admin fee)

    Book Now

  • Bryde with support from Adam Thorn

    Saturday 10 October | 7:30pm

    Bryde aka Sarah Howells, is a woman and an electric guitar, playing fierce and fragile songs. Swaying from vulnerable to uncompromising within one verse and chorus, Bryde’s music is honest and furiously authentic.

    Fans have compared the music to acts as varied as Stevie Nicks, The Cranberries, Jeff Buckley, Lucy Dacus and even Taylor Swift.

    Tickets: £15 (plus £1 admin fee)

    Book Now

  • Cymuned Gwy Premier Performance

    Sunday 11 October | 1pm

    Music commissioned by Wyeside, to mark our 50th anniversary

    Cymuned Gwy is a new collaborative project featuring Nia Lynn (vocals, percussion and harmonium), Toby Hay (guitar) and Aidan Thorne (double bass). The trio has written music inspired by and celebrating the 50th anniversary of the Wyeside, the beauty of its surrounding landscape, the importance of the River Wye with remarkable stories of our local community. 

    Through both Welsh and English language Cymuned Gwy celebrates Brycheiniog’s lingual heritage and represents today’s bilingual community. The music weaves all these elements together and is premiered this weekend. 

    Tickets: £5 (plus £1 admin fee)

    Book Now

  • Netty the Nettle: A Storytime Adventure with Author Georgia Wickham

    Sunday 11 October | 2pm

    Join children's author Georgia Wickham for a special reading of Netty the Nettle, a heart-warming story about courage, kindness and celebrating what makes us unique.

    Set in a sunny South Wales garden, the story follows Netty, a little nettle who feels left out until she discovers that being different can be her greatest strength.

    Perfect for young children and families, this interactive storytelling session will be followed by the opportunity to purchase signed copies of the book.

    Tickets: Free

    Book Now

  • Robin Hood (U)

    Sunday 11 October | 2pm

    Animation | Adventure | Comedy | Family | Musical | Romance

    The story of the legendary British outlaw portrayed with the characters as anthropomorphic animals.

    Running Time: 83 mins | Flashing Images: None

    Tickets: £5 (plus £1 admin fee)

    Book Now

  • Alive in the Apiary

    Sunday 11 October | 4pm

    Documentary

    This short documentary follows Richard, a man who fell ill at the age of 32 and spent the next 34 years battling an autoimmune disease before finding that beekeeping would change his life forever.

    Tickets: Free

    Book Now

  • Builth Wells & Beulah YFC’s present ‘Checkmate’

    Sunday 11 October | 5pm

    ‘Checkmate’ brings together the game of chess, and the images of the silent movie era. Set on a life size chess board, we also see elements of old black and white movies that feature Charlie Chaplin. His character weaves his way through the action of the chess board, sometime observing, occasionally being involved in the action.

    Written by David Price and directed by Lynne Jones and David Price, Young Farmers from these two local clubs recently joined forces for the Entertainment competition held earlier this year. They now bring the fun and spectacle of this production to Wyeside during this weekend of celebrations!

    Tickets: £5 (plus £1 admin fee)

    Book Now

  • Film Club: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest (15)

    Sunday 11 October | 5pm

    A criminal avoids prison by being committed to a mental institution, where he decides to lead a rebellion.

    Running Time: 134 mins | Flashing Images: None

    Content Warning: scenes of violence, suicide and discrimination, as well as rape references, may upset some viewers.

    Tickets: £5 (plus £1 admin fee)

    Book Now

  • MPYT 'teaser' Rumpelstiltskin

    Sunday 11 October | 7:30pm

    MPYT offers a tantalising autumn morsel of the theatre harvest to come. Can you guess the Name of the Helper? Well, it's Rumpelstiltskin obviously.

    Tickets: £5 (plus £1 admin fee)

    Book Now

  • People's Vote

    Sunday 11 October | 7:45pm

    We gave you the option to vote for which film you would like to see as our last film of the Birthday Weekend.

    Invoke some mystery and be surprised by the mystery!

    Voting closes on September 13.

    Tickets: £5 (plus £1 admin fee)

    Book Now

Wyeside Arts Centre

Situated in the heart of Builth Wells, on Castle Street, along the main High Street, within easy walking distance from the bus station. Wyeside is situated on the bank of the River Wye, an iconic Grade II listed building.

PHONE - 01982 552 555
